details: On June 17, 2026, President Trump signed a peace Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) with Iran, aiming to de-escalate the ongoing conflict and facilitate the reopening of the Strait of Hormuz. This geopolitical development was initially perceived positively by markets, leading to a rally in risk assets, including Bitcoin, which briefly surged to $66,315. The agreement was expected to reduce geopolitical risk and lower oil prices, thus lifting broader market sentiment.

title: US-Iran Peace MoU Signed, Briefly Boosting Crypto Risk Appetite

details: The Federal Reserve, under new Chair Kevin Warsh, held interest rates steady at 3.50%-3.75% during its June 17, 2026, meeting. However, the decision was accompanied by a hawkish surprise: nine of the eighteen Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) officials now project at least one rate hike in 2026, and the policy statement removed previous dovish guidance. This unexpected hawkish shift overshadowed the positive geopolitical news from the US-Iran deal, causing Bitcoin to drop to $64,339 and triggering over $122 million in liquidations for Bitcoin and Ethereum, amplifying fear and leading to a broader altcoin plunge in the cryptocurrency market.
